title: Microsoft Purview DLP: rules to auto-resolve and tag alerts
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned rules and roadmap targets, and distinguishes them from existing alert management. The corrected Purview dashboard permissions match Microsoft Learn; searches confirmed the narrowly stated gaps in documentation for the new rules.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans rule-based alert tagging and auto-resolution in Microsoft Purview DLP.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - Rule-based tagging and auto-resolution of alerts based on business needs of the customer.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether the planned alert tags are the existing Defender incident custom tags.

Read roadmap, alert-investigation-learn and Defender DLP investigation; current incident tags are documented, but no connection to the planned alert tags is stated.

claims.claim: Existing alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.
claims.quote: Alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.

claims.claim: DLP alerts can be investigated in the Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard, subject to the stated alert-tuning condition.
claims.quote: When the built-in DLP alert tuning rule is disabled, you can manage and respond to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) alerts and incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Defender XDR for investigating and managing DLP alerts.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard is the recommended location for investigating and managing DLP alerts.

claims.claim: Existing DLP alerts can also be investigated in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: DLP alerts can be investigated and managed in the Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard and in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The documented Purview dashboard procedure has an analyst set Status to Resolved after taking the required action.
claims.quote: After you take the required action for the alert, set the Status of the alert to Resolved.

claims.claim: The built-in Defender DLP alert tuning rule took effect in early October 2026.
claims.quote: A built-in alert tuning rule for DLP signals took effect in early October 2026.

claims.claim: The built-in Defender tuning rule converts DLP signals to behaviors instead of alerts.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Defender XDR, the rule sets these signals as behaviors instead of alerts, so they don't generate alerts or appear in the incident queue.

claims.claim: Microsoft says to disable the built-in tuning rule to continue seeing DLP signals as Defender XDR alerts.
claims.quote: To continue seeing DLP signals as alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR, disable the rule in Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning.

claims.claim: Access to the Purview DLP alert management dashboard requires Manage alerts plus DLP Compliance Management or View-Only DLP Compliance Management.
claims.quote:
To access the DLP alert management dashboard, you need the Manage alerts role and either of these two roles:
- DLP Compliance Management
- View-Only DLP Compliance Management

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn states that the existing DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.
claims.quote: The DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn also says audit log retention configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.
claims.quote: Your organization's audit log retention policy configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents associating custom tags with existing DLP incidents in the Defender portal.
claims.quote: Associate custom tags to DLP incidents and filter by them.

claims.claim: Single-event alert configuration is available with the DLP subscriptions listed as E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, E3, G3, E5, G5.
claims.quote: Single-event alert configuration: All organizations with a DLP subscription (E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, E3, G3, E5, G5) can configure policies to generate an alert for every time a triggering activity occurs.
